I agree with the coverage method: zero unresolved mandatory families/interactions, full source/identity disposition, no unimplemented mandatory feature hidden as Unsupported, representative witnesses only for genuinely equivalent validated semantics, and pure internal rules tested through their owning operation.

Please review these concrete amendments before I freeze the draft. Actual read-only host inspection finds Intel i5-4590 (4 physical/4 logical cores), 16 GB installed RAM (~16,683,164 KiB visible), Windows10 x64 build19045, Samsung870 EVO SATA SSD on local NTFS, PowerShell7.6.9/.NET10.0.14. Retained timings used this host. Use this existing machine as the reference rather than requiring an unowned six-core/NVMe machine. C#9 warnings-as-errors; optimized HEADLESS_TESTS/DECENNIUM_TEST_ONLY build, exact compiler/options/DLL hashes, identical validation semantics. These are headless targets, not Unity/IL2CPP frame-time claims.

Your 32 persistent actors/12 encounter participants/5 controlled actors and authorized logical views,4 authored areas×4096 valid anchors,256 objects,512 lots,16 jobs/8 lawful progressing jobs,256 settlements in a mixed advance are a useful bounded minimum range, not gameplay caps or new party/roster rules. Add at most256 active effect instances (16 per actor) and define exact dense-End events in each manifest. Keep the10-minute and24-hour workload budgets at1.5/3sec and3/6sec p95/max, interactive query25/75ms, move/ordinary interaction50/150ms, tactical75/250ms. No workload can game a result by empty capacity or omitted pending work.

For useful long-session coverage I propose history tiers128,1024 and10,000 committed receipts, not a ceiling just over twice the current463-command path. Require lawful varied histories, exact causal validation and continuation, no dropped history/unreviewed compaction. Warm strict restore p95/max:5/8sec,10/15sec,30/45sec respectively; process-cold10,000 tier40/60sec with launch separately recorded. Save at10,000 receipts1/2sec including normal backup/flush; maximum canonical save64MiB and process peak private bytes2GiB at the upper envelope. Post-GC20-cycle retained growth<=64MiB in a separate diagnostic run. These are prospective engineering targets requiring future work if missed, never a statement that the present engine meets them or a retroactive module failure.

Retain three independent batches,100 interactive samples per named operation/seat/workload (not pooling different endpoints to hide a slow one),20 bulk/save/restore samples, nearest-rank p95, all batches pass p95 AND maxima, no cherry-picked reruns, no forced GC in latency windows. Pin workload outcomes/event composition first and require deterministic/authority/rollback correctness before timing. Cap exceptions must retain source legality and be reviewed explicitly, never replace missing required capabilities with easier fixtures.

Please agree or identify concrete adjustments. The actual49-row capability obligations and frozen source inventory will be in the written contract. No benchmark, source contract for Consecration, runtime or module is being started.

items.text:
**I agree with the amendments for the UR-01/UR-04 draft.** Use the inspected i5-4590, 16 GB, Windows 10 build 19045, SATA SSD/NTFS host with PowerShell 7.6.9 and .NET 10.0.14 as the reference. Pin the optimized C# 9 warnings-as-errors build, compiler options, conditional symbols, DLL hashes, and actual timed entry points. These are prospective headless targets. The accepted INT-03/P1 timing disposition and all other exact module acceptances stand.

The **10,000-receipt tier** is a meaningful long-session target. I agree with warm strict-restore p95/max of **5/8, 10/15, and 30/45 seconds** at 128, 1,024, and 10,000 receipts, and **40/60 seconds** for process-cold strict restore at 10,000. Keep the **1/2-second** upper-tier save target, **64 MiB** canonical save limit, **2 GiB** peak process private-bytes limit, and **64 MiB** retained managed growth limit. The interactive and advance budgets stand as proposed.

Before freezing, make four points explicit in the written contract:

1. **Define each workload by its actual contents.** Declare controlled actors and authorized logical views separately. Count party actors within the actor total, and require the encounter roster, jobs, and effects to arise lawfully. For each dense End and bulk-advance case, pin the named pending work, due-event counts and order, expected settlements, and resulting state. Define what counts toward the 256 active effects and disclose any source-authorized overlap or exclusion. The envelope establishes qualification coverage without changing party, roster, or effect rules.
2. **Pin the persistence measurement boundary.** Count committed receipts across the actual causal history and report canonical bytes, schema/profile, and retained history at each tier. Time save through normal backup, commit, and flush. Time restore through full causal validation and publication of usable state, then verify continuation. For process-cold samples, record launch separately and disclose normal OS file-cache behavior. Preserve the supported-save matrix. Any future compaction proposal needs its own review of causality and compatibility.
3. **Make every batch independently auditable.** Apply p95 and maximum to each named operation, seat where applicable, workload, and batch. With nearest-rank p95, the 19th sorted sample controls a 20-sample batch and the 95th controls a 100-sample batch. Retain every sample and failed batch. Count peak private bytes for the full headless process, including the host. For the separate 20-cycle diagnostic, define a stabilized post-GC baseline and measure retained live managed bytes after cycle 20 using the same collection procedure.
4. **Keep contract status and qualification status separate.** UR-01 closes only when the published matrix accounts for all 49 workstreams and has zero unresolved mandatory families or required interactions without evidence. UR-04 qualifies only after all three batches meet correctness, p95, maximum, and applicable memory limits on the pinned host. If a proposed workload cannot be populated lawfully, record the precise conflict and review the replacement explicitly. The required capability stays open until qualifying evidence exists.

This is agreement on the draft criteria. No benchmark or gameplay execution occurred. Implementation remains paused, and the Consecration source/API contract remains held and unstarted.

These are NEW forward targets, not retroactive rejection of accepted module timings and not measured passes. items.text:
**Proposed pre-Unity contract:** complete the reusable C# engine against a frozen inventory of required gameplay capabilities and qualify it within the operating envelope below. UR-01 and UR-04 can become **specified, pending implementation and qualification** once the published contract is reviewed. The first Unity integration remains a development/TEST_ONLY integration unless separately promoted. The accepted 49-workstream map, its 120 direct edges, and its original acceptance criteria remain the baseline. [Accepted implementation map and status](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/tree/65e6153a8c1511290bd68d47c5ce6a636ecec821/docs/unity)

## UR-01 — Capability coverage

Build a versioned coverage matrix beneath the existing 49 rows. Freeze the source corpus at named revisions and identify the source registry, operative rule records, accepted amendments, and precedence used to resolve conflicts. Give every operative rule family a stable ID, a primary workstream, cross-references to its consuming workstreams, and a disposition. Require every C# obligation in the map to trace to one or more family records. Pure Unity and product deliverables keep their later-phase disposition.

| Completion criterion | Required evidence |
|---|---|
| **Complete inventory and disposition** | Account for every operative family in the frozen corpus. Distinguish required and accepted, required and open, unresolved source authority, and later work under an explicit scope decision. A required mechanic with missing source or implementation stays open. Preserve original catalogue identities and qualified exclusions. |
| **Source-bound semantic contract** | Bind eligibility, authority, inputs, costs, timing/order, RNG ownership, targeting/geometry where applicable, result, lifecycle, and failure behavior. Resolve applicable cross-system interactions and persistence semantics. Use Codex/GPT delegation for routine resolution and escalate irreconcilable source conflicts or material product-scope decisions. |
| **Reusable implementation** | Exercise each required operation through its normal public command, query, or owning operation for an internal rule. Queries and discovery must reflect the admitted authority and available choices where the contract requires them. All interfaces share the same resolver. Persistent effects and pending choices use the authoritative state, restore and replay paths. Pure rules exercised by an owning operation do not need standalone commands. |
| **Semantic witnesses** | For each distinct mechanism, retain a lawful positive witness, a meaningful denial with the expected cost/RNG/state behavior, and a boundary witness for each distinct settlement branch required by the contract. Add pending-save or retry witnesses where the lifecycle can be interrupted, resumed, or redelivered. Derive expected results independently from the source. Group cases that prove the same mechanism. |
| **Cross-system closure** | Require connected scenarios for exploration → combat → loot/custody → preparation/work → continued exploration, plus required variants involving concurrent work, reaction or condition timing, save/reload at a pending choice, and authority/privacy. The accepted INT-03 loop and exact module evidence count toward this matrix. Add evidence only for required behavior they leave uncovered. |
| **Family-based catalogue qualification** | Validate every in-scope identity’s actual handler, complete parameter bindings, source revision, access, eligibility, authority, and visibility. Share runtime witnesses only where identity differences stay within the same validated contract. A distinct resolver branch, outcome, resource lifecycle, targeting restriction, or interaction needs its own witness even when it shares a handler. |

The completion rule is **zero unresolved mandatory families and zero required interaction rows without qualifying evidence**. Report that alongside the named supported profile/save matrix. Keep workstream status, evidence strength, content authority, and first-integration content selection as independent fields. This makes closure finite without using either test count or catalogue size as a proxy for completeness. [Historical rule map](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/65e6153a8/docs/unity/evidence/2026-11-03-rule-map/RULE_MAP.json) · [Development brief](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/65e6153a8/docs/unity/DEVELOPMENT_BRIEF.md)

## UR-04 — Proposed operating envelope

These are **new forward qualification targets**. The retained INT-03 review reports Default restore p95 of **4.330 seconds** on the first run and **3.851 seconds** on the accepted repeat. The r223/r242 longer-history results were about **6.67/6.65 seconds**. Preserve those results and the original per-run ruling. The new targets below reserve more time for strict restore as history grows and keep interactive commands on a separate, tighter budget. [INT-03/P1 final review, §4](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/65e6153a8/docs/unity/evidence/2026-11-13-int03-strict-restoration/GPT_FINAL_REVIEW.md)

| Dimension | Proposed required qualification range |
|---|---|
| **Actors and views** | Up to **32 persistent actors**, **12 active encounter participants**, **5 party actors**, and **5 authorized logical views** exercised serially. Network transport and simultaneous clients remain later work. |
| **World and resources** | Up to **4 authored areas**, **4,096 cells per area**, **256 persistent world objects**, and **512 inventory lots** across the session. Exercise cross-area continuity and a populated active area rather than allocating empty capacity. |
| **Work and scheduler** | Up to **16 live job records**, **8 concurrently progressing where lawful**, and **256 due settlements** in one mixed-work advance. Exercise a 10-minute active mixed-work window and a 24-hour sparse world advance. |
| **History and persistence** | Exercise **128-, 512-, and 1,024-receipt** histories. At 1,024, propose a **32 MiB maximum canonical save**, including associated causal history. Use meaningful, lawful histories with active and completed records. Maintain the existing supported save/profile matrix separately. |
| **Memory** | At the upper workload, cap headless process peak private bytes at **1 GiB**. After 20 repeated load/continue/dispose cycles, post-GC live managed memory must stay within **64 MiB** of the stabilized baseline. Measure on a separate diagnostic run so forced collections cannot improve latency results. |

Treat these as a **minimum range the engine must qualify**, not new gameplay caps. The benchmark matrix should include one combined upper-envelope workload and dense tactical and due-event cases. A source-imposed limit stays in force, and independently legal sessions beyond this range carry no performance claim under this contract.

| Public headless operation | Warm p95 | Hard maximum |
|---|---:|---:|
| One seat’s filtered view, discovery, or command query, measured separately | **25 ms** | **75 ms** |
| Paid exploration edge or ordinary interaction | **50 ms** | **150 ms** |
| Tactical action, reaction resolution, or End with due local consequences | **75 ms** | **250 ms** |
| Advance 10 game minutes with concurrent active work and interruptions | **1.5 s** | **3 s** |
| Advance 24 game hours in the sparse world case, with actual due work and at most 256 settlements | **3 s** | **6 s** |
| Public save to local SSD, including ordinary commit/backup handling at 1,024 receipts | **1 s** | **2 s** |
| Strict restore through the public API at 128 / 512 / 1,024 receipts | **5 / 15 / 30 s** | **8 / 22 / 45 s** |
| First public strict restore in a fresh process at 1,024 receipts | **40 s** | **60 s** |

The advance targets are for two pinned workload shapes. They do not promise that every 24-hour command has equivalent work. Define the due-event composition and expected settlements before measuring, and publish event counts alongside elapsed time. The restore targets include strict causal validation and publication of the restored state. A shallow decode or a cached validated snapshot cannot satisfy them.

**Reference machine and protocol.** Use one pinned Windows x64 desktop with six physical cores or better, 16 GiB RAM, and a local NVMe SSD as the reference class. Record the exact CPU, OS build, RAM, storage, power profile, collector, compiler, runtime version, Release build, and assembly hashes. Pin the actual machine and runtime in the published contract before qualification. The reference class is a proposed planning assumption, not a verified description of the current machine or a Unity player minimum.

- Run **three independent batches** with fresh processes and identical pinned inputs. In each batch, collect **100 measured samples per interactive operation class** after 10 unscored warm-ups, and **20 samples per save, restore tier, and long-advance workload** after two unscored warm-ups. For process-cold restore, take **20 fresh-process first-call samples per batch**, with normal OS filesystem caching explicitly disclosed. Time process launch separately.
- Use nearest-rank p95 and publish p50, p95, maximum, and raw samples **per batch and workload**. All three batches must meet both thresholds. Start each measured mutation from the intended legitimate state. Place reset/setup outside the timed call, but keep ordinary runtime GC, file I/O, validation, and due-event processing inside it. Retain failed batches. An instrumentation failure can invalidate a batch only with a recorded cause and replacement run.
- Before any timing result can pass, require correct outcomes, identical canonical checkpoints and RNG for equivalent histories, exact filtered views and ordered discovery where applicable, and successful strict continuation. Denials, corrupt or forged saves, and invalid authority must preserve state according to their contracts. Crashes, timeouts, missing samples, skipped work, nondeterministic results, or timing/memory ceiling breaches fail qualification. Retain diagnostics for CPU/GC, allocation and peak memory, bytes, receipts, commands, and due events so a miss identifies a workload and boundary.

The tradeoff is a **responsive headless command path with seconds-scale bulk advances and a separately budgeted strict load**. The 1,024-receipt tier deliberately goes beyond the accepted 463-command Ferry path. Its 30-second warm p95 is a first-integration engineering target. Any tighter player-facing load budget belongs in an explicit later product contract. [TAC-10 final acceptance](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/65e6153a8/docs/unity/evidence/2026-11-16-tac10-ferry-wraith-runtime/FINAL_ACCEPTANCE.md)

I read the accepted map, machine status, development brief, and retained INT-03 timing review. These are planning proposals with no measured passes. No repository edits, benchmarks, or gameplay execution occurred. Implementation remains paused, and the amended Consecration contract remains held and unstarted.
